title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Open rather than dense POM frameworks are favored by sterically bulky countercations or by intrinsically porous POM secondary building units, whose internal pores propagate into framework channels.
explanation: The authors identify dense packing from extra metal ions as a design problem and present two remedies: large-hindrance cations that enlarge voids, and porous clusters such as {P5W30} and {P8W48}. Later sections show these rings and Preyssler anions accounting for a large share of open tungstate frameworks, with channels often occupied by cations, water, or added guests.
scope: POM-based all-inorganic frameworks, especially polyoxotungstates using {P5W30} or {P8W48}.
conditions: Porous SBUs are linked by alkali or transition-metal cations; bulky organic cations such as tetramethylammonium can occupy the resulting channels.
caveats: Bulky cations enlarge or occupy voids but can also fill channels, so they do not automatically yield guest-accessible porosity.
